sections.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights
sections.abstract: For the closure of nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficients bounded in modulus by an integer height, the authors prove connectedness holds exactly at pronic heights and establish extensive component results at other heights.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the nonreal-root closure is connected iff the height is q(q−1), q≥2; otherwise it has at least five components, with further component results and double-zero conjectures addressed.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Integer polynomials of arbitrary degree with coefficients of absolute value at most an integer h≥1; closure in the complex plane of their nonreal roots.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a long new preprint (45 pages plus a 35-page supplement), not yet independently reviewed; some exceptional nonpronic heights remain unresolved in the component-count statements.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A complete arithmetic classification of connectedness, named prior observations/conjectures resolved at particular heights, cross-listing between complex analysis and number theory, a Zenodo computational supplement, and a Wolfram MathWorld summary.
sections.comment: 45 pages, 8 figures, with a 35-page supplement (80 pages in all); computational companion DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24117729

sections.title: Phase transitions in the hard-wall large deviations for the Gaussian free field
sections.abstract: For the discrete Gaussian free field in dimension d≥3 constrained above a moving hard wall on a dilated bounded domain, the authors identify a critical window where collective displacement and suppression of local violations contribute together to a sharp variational rate.
sections.claimed_result: In the critical window h_N(β)^2=g_0(4 log N+log log N+2β), the normalized log hard-wall probability converges to the negative infimum of a functional combining Dirichlet energy and an exponential potential; moving-speed asymptotics are also given on both sides.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Centered GFF on Z^d, d≥3, with simple-random-walk Green-function covariance; D is a bounded Lipschitz domain and D_N=(ND)∩Z^d.
sections.unique_caveat: The results concern d≥3 and the stated domain/scaling regime; the analogous critical-window rate for random interlacements remains open.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A sharp variational asymptotic in a specified transition window, off-window regimes, and a connection to random-interlacement cover levels; cross-listed in probability and mathematical physics.

sections.title: The distribution of small gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
sections.abstract: Using an unconditional variant of Montgomery’s pair-correlation method, the author improves the explicit constant in Selberg’s theorem on the proportion of consecutive zeta zeros with unusually small gaps, showing that λ₀=0.7892 is admissible.
sections.claimed_result: For a positive proportion of consecutive nontrivial zeta zeros, the ordinate gap is at most 2πλ₀/log γ_n with λ₀=0.7892<4/5, unconditionally.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Nontrivial zeros in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity; unconditional result concerning a positive proportion, not all gaps.
sections.unique_caveat: The result does not determine the full gap distribution or establish the bound for every consecutive zero pair.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives a checkable unconditional improvement over the best explicit constant it cites (1−2.36×10⁻⁶) and states the admissible value 0.7892.

sections.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
sections.abstract: The author rules out a simplicial triangulation of the three-torus with 13 vertices, narrowing the minimum possible number of vertices to 14 or 15.
sections.claimed_result: There is no simplicial triangulation of T³ on 13 vertices; with existing lower bounds and a 15-vertex construction, 14≤v(T³)≤15.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite simplicial triangulations of the closed three-torus; the contradiction uses the Novik–Swartz g₂ inequality and properties of small simplicial complexes.
sections.unique_caveat: The result does not decide whether a 14-vertex triangulation exists or whether the known 15-vertex construction is minimal.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It closes the first unresolved vertex count after the established lower bound, combines face-number inequalities, fundamental groups and Alexander duality, and is cross-listed in topology and combinatorics; MathWorld records the 14–15 range.

sections.title: Regularity of Q-valued C¹ harmonic functions with applications to stable minimal hypersurfaces
sections.abstract: The author proves Hölder regularity and branch-set structure for Q-valued C¹ functions harmonic on their regular set, then applies these results to stable minimal hypersurfaces under small-slope and singular-set hypotheses.
sections.claimed_result: The derivative is locally Dirichlet-minimizing and shares the branch set; the function is C¹,α with a countably (n−2)-rectifiable branch set for n≥3 and a discrete branch set for n=2. A small-Lipschitz multivalued graph satisfying the stated stable-hypersurface hypotheses is also C¹,α.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Locally harmonicity on the regular set. The hypersurface application assumes a two-sided, properly immersed stable minimal graph, locally finite H^(n−2) singular measure, and sufficiently small Lipschitz constant.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusions depend on the multivalued and stability hypotheses and do not assert regularity for arbitrary singular minimal hypersurfaces.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Specific regularity and rectifiability claims with an application bridging geometric measure theory and elliptic analysis; cross-listed in differential geometry and PDE.

sections.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
sections.abstract: Near the standard invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces, the author proves that sufficiently small smooth deformations preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness arise only from holomorphic automorphisms and constant rescaling.
sections.claimed_result: For a fixed standard polarization on a compact Hermitian symmetric space, sufficiently small deformations satisfying vanishing of a finite consecutive block of canonically twisted Bergman coefficients are the pullback of the reference metric by a polarized holomorphic automorphism, up to a positive constant.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact Hermitian symmetric space with fixed invariant positive polarization; the deformation remains positive and small in a suitable C^(s,α) norm, and a sufficiently long finite block of Bergman coefficients vanishes.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is local and relies on the symmetric-space setting and fixed polarization; the authors conjecture an extension to general compact polarized Kähler manifolds.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A local rigidity theorem spanning differential geometry, complex analysis and representation theory, with a finite-coefficient criterion near the standard metric.
